Company description:
Epiroc is a leading productivity partner for the mining, infrastructure and natural resources industries. Withcutting-edge technology, Epiroc develops and produces innovative drill rigs, rock excavation and constructionequipment, and provides world-class service and consumables. The company was founded in Stockholm,Sweden, and has passionate people supporting and collaborating with customers in more than 150 countries.Learn more at www.epirocgroup.com.
Job description:We’re looking for a Product Owner – AI & Test Engineering to join our SW Platform organization. We’re responsible for the machine platform that Epiroc’s mining and construction equipment runs on.
 In this role, AI is at the heart of what you do. You’ll help shape how software developers across all of Epiroc use AI in their daily work, and how AI changes the way we test and verify our software.
 Are you curious about how AI is changing software development? Do you enjoy collaborating with people across teams and helping turn needs into clear priorities? Would you like to help build something new from the start, with an impact across the whole company? Then we’d love to hear from you.
 A stream in the making
 AI & Test Engineering is a new product stream in our platform organisation. The teams are being built right now, and their setup, size and exact scope aren’t finalised yet. As Product Owner, you’ll have a real opportunity to influence how the stream takes shape, together with the teams, your manager and the Chief Product Owner.
 Your mission
 As Product Owner you’re responsible for the AI & Test Engineering product stream, where AI is the main focus. The stream is planned to cover two areas:
  AI Software Factory: exploring and introducing AI-supported, agentic ways of working across the software development lifecycle, for all software developers at Epiroc.
 AI-driven Test & Integration: using AI to rethink how we test and integrate platform software, together with test frameworks, simulation, a software-defined lab and system testing.
  
You connect the teams with their stakeholders. For the AI Software Factory, these are software developers and development teams across Epiroc’s divisions and sites. For Test & Integration, they are mainly the internal teams that develop and deliver on the platform.
 You’re responsible for the product backlog in Jira and the roadmap. By listening to stakeholders and understanding their needs, you help translate them into clear epics and user stories and support the teams in focusing on what creates the most value.
 You keep up with how AI in software development is evolving and help turn new possibilities into practical value for developers and testers.
 You work closely with the Scrum Masters and Tech Leads, collaborate with our architects and work closely with the Chief Product Owner on the overall platform roadmap. You also take part in cross-team planning together with the other product streams. You’ll report to a team manager in the SW Platform organization and be part of a supportive team where knowledge sharing and learning are encouraged.
Profile description:Your profile
  You have experience as a Product Owner or in a similar role, for example product manager, test lead, technical project lead or requirements owner, in a software development environment.
 You have a genuine interest in AI and how it can support software development and testing, and you may already use AI tools in your own work.
 You’re familiar with agile ways of working such as Scrum and with tools like Jira.
 You enjoy working with a broad range of stakeholders and helping new ways of working spread across an organization.
 It’s a plus if you have experience with AI-assisted or agentic software development, AI in testing, test automation, CI/CD or simulation.
 You speak Swedish and you’re fluent in English, both written and spoken.
  
As a person, you’re curious, structured, communicative and collaborative. You’re comfortable when not everything is decided yet, and you enjoy helping to create structure together with others. You build trusting relationships with stakeholders, help the teams find focus and like to keep learning.
 We know that great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this role sounds interesting, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We welcome applicants of all genders and backgrounds and believe diverse teams build better products.
 Location
 The role is based in Örebro, Sweden. We work hybrid, with at least three days a week in the office.
 Application and contacts
 Please send your application, including CV and personal letter, by creating an account in our recruitment system as soon as possible but no later than 27th of November.
 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the position may be filled before last application date. Please note that, due to the current regulations, we will only consider applications received through our system and not via email or social media.

jobs.description:
The Education Office (EdO) is one of SSE’s Professional Services units and consists of around 58 colleagues. As a central part of the SSE journey, we support and develop key academic services for students and stakeholders across our BSc, MSc, and PhD programs. Our work spans assessment, program management, scholarships, international collaborations, academic support, central course and exam coordination, as well as degrees and certificates.
We offer you
A diverse role at one of the top business schools in Europe with ambitious students and staff in a dynamic, academic environment. This role is ideal for a highly organized, people-oriented person who enjoys complex processes.
The role
We are looking for Admissions coordinator for our BSc programs. The successful candidate will belong to a team of Admissions & Program management at Education Office, reporting to Group Manager of that team.
Your tasks include, but are not limited to:
Coordinating application and admissions process for the BSc programs, ensuring an efficient, accurate and applicant-focused process.
Assessing applications, including eligibility, qualifications and supporting documentation, and participating actively in the selection of candidates.
Guiding prospective students and applicants regarding SSE, the BSc programs, admissions requirements and the application process.
Collaborating with faculty, and other internal and external stakeholders involved in admissions.
Contributing to recruitment and conversion activities for prospective and admitted students, including information sessions, events and other applicant-facing activities.
Supporting the Program Manager for the BSc in Business & Economics with diverse program-related tasks and activities, in accordance with the agreed division of responsibilities and based on the needs of the program.
Contributing to the continuous development of admissions processes, systems and ways of working, including the use of digital tools and AI where relevant.
Working in a dynamic organization where priorities, processes and responsibilities may evolve. You should therefore be comfortable adapting to change, taking on new tasks and contributing to developing new ways of working.
Occasional travel and participation in events outside regular office activities may occur.

Your profile
As Admissions Coordinator, you will be coordinating admissions process and processing applications and enquiries, often within fixed deadlines. You therefore need to be structured, detail-oriented and comfortable taking responsibility for processes from start to finish. You are proactive, flexible and able to prioritize while maintaining a high level of accuracy and service.
At the same time, admissions process is highly collaborative, and you enjoy working closely with colleagues, faculty and other stakeholders. The position involves contact with prospective students and applicants. You therefore have strong interpersonal and communication skills and can explain sometimes complex admissions requirements in a clear, professional and service-minded way. You are also comfortable handling challenging cases and communicating decisions consistently and respectfully. You are comfortable interpreting admissions requirements, assessing applicants and documentation against established criteria, and applying rules and procedures consistently.
Qualifications:
An academic education
Experience of, or a strong understanding of, admissions processes within Swedish higher education.
Experience of working with Swedish and international high school qualifications
Swedish and English, both spoken and written.
An interest in how generative AI and digital tools can support efficient and high-quality admissions processes.

Meritorious:
Previous experience working with admissions in Swedish higher education, particularly BSc admissions.
International experience or previous experience working in an international environment is an asset.
Good knowledge of Swedish higher-education admissions processes, eligibility requirements, merit rating and selection principles.
Experience assessing Swedish and international upper-secondary qualifications and supporting documentation.
Previous experience working in NyA and/or Ladok, or other systems used in higher-education admissions.
Previous experience working with CRM or application-management systems.

Other

Join the Revolution in Commercial Vehicle Tech at Coretura!
Our AI Lab builds the shared platform that teams across Coretura use to develop and run AI products safely and reliably. We're looking for a senior software engineer to help design, build and run it.
What you’ll do
You will work with the AI Lab to set the platform's technical direction, and take on a large share of the hands-on work yourself. Together, you'll build the platform that gives teams access to AI models across providers, manages and retrieves the data their AI products rely on, and provides the harnesses agents are built and run in. You'll also build agents yourself, and the observability that shows whether an AI product is giving the right answers, not just whether it's running.
Beyond that, your work will include:

Security and safety by level: controls and evaluations that scale with how autonomous an AI system is and how safety-critical its use is, from everyday AI tools to autonomous agents, with prompt injection defences built in. The higher the level, the more a system has to prove before release and the more closely it's monitored once live. You'll build this together with our Security Hub.

Cost and resilience: usage metering built into the platform so teams can see what their AI products consume, and recovery tested for each AI product as a whole (model, knowledge base, prompts and tool integrations), not just the servers it runs on.

AI assets as code: prompts, agent definitions, model versions and evaluation datasets, versioned and released through automated pipelines. They change often and any change can shift how a product behaves, so every change is automatically tested, evaluated and traceable before it ships.

Build to discover, then share what you learn. When we need to know whether an approach works, you build a working version, then use it to help colleagues across Coretura understand what works, what doesn't and why. As a senior engineer, you'll combine those findings with your own experience to help set where the platform goes next. You'll use AI coding agents in your own daily work and help other engineers adopt them safely. You'll also review designs and code, mentor the engineers around you, and hand over ownership of components as they're ready for it.
You'll report to the AI Lab Lead and work closely with our Digital Architect and the teams behind our developer and data platforms.
What you bring
A solid background in software engineering, but we care far more about what you've done than how long you've been doing it. You've owned a production system end to end, including its roadmap, incidents and costs, and you've handed parts of it over to other engineers along the way.
You're comfortable with:

Using AI coding agents as a normal part of how you write code, with work you can show for it

Building AI applications that people can rely on: agents, retrieval (RAG), model APIs and gateways, along with the evaluations that show they behave as intended

Defining cloud infrastructure in code and shipping through CI/CD as part of how you build software, with the observability to see how it behaves once it's running

Practical security, from least privilege and secrets management to prompt injection defences

Writing well-tested, maintainable code in whatever language the problem calls for, and picking up a new one when you need to

You look for more efficient ways to build and run things, bring structure to an unclear situation without locking it down too early, and can explain a trade-off so that engineers, security and leadership all understand it. Fluent English is a must.
Why Coretura?
We're a joint venture between Volvo Group and Daimler Truck, building a shared software platform for the next generation of commercial vehicles. We're a young company with very little legacy to work around, backed by two of the world's largest commercial vehicle manufacturers.
The AI platform serves teams across the company, so your work will directly affect how they build and ship software.
If this sounds like the work you want to do, we look forward to your application.
Next steps Ready to build the future of commercial vehicles?
We review applications on a continuous basis, so don’t wait to submit yours!
Last application date: 4th of December 2026.
Questions? Don’t hesitate to reach out to Frida Greve, frida.greve@coretura.com if you have any questions regarding the position.
Please note we do not accept any applications via email.

jobs.description:
About the Center for wellbeing, welfare and happiness and research area
Wellbeing research examines how people experience and evaluate their lives, what enables them to thrive, and how individuals, organizations and societies can contribute to better lives. The field brings together perspectives from psychology, economics and behavioural science to understand different dimensions of wellbeing, including happiness, meaning in life and psychological richness. At the Center for Wellbeing, Welfare and Happiness (CWWH), we connect these questions to the development of knowledge that can inform policy and practice.
A central methodological challenge is how to capture the richness of people’s experiences through reliable and valid measures. Advances in natural language processing and large language models offer opportunities to complement traditional rating scales with systematic analyses of people’s own descriptions of their lives, emotions and experiences. This research combines wellbeing science, psychometrics and computational methods to investigate what language-based assessments can reveal about wellbeing, how they relate to established measures, and how they can capture differences between people and changes over time. The position will contribute to developing and validating these approaches, with relevance to the center’s research in Sweden and across countries.
The role
The postdoc will develop an independent research line on the measurement of wellbeing beyond traditional rating scales, with a focus on natural language (open-ended responses, text and speech) analyzed with computational methods, including large language models.
The postdoc will contribute to the center's work on wellbeing in Sweden and across nations, co-author with center researchers, and connect CWWH to international collaborators and funding opportunities. The role also includes active participation in the center's outreach, such as media, public lectures and events. 
Your profile
The applicants must hold a PhD by time of employment and to be eligible, applicants must have obtained their doctoral degree within the three years preceding the date of employment. This period may be extended only where special circumstances apply. Professional proficiency in English (written and spoken) is a requirement. We expect the candidate to relocate to Stockholm. 
Qualifications
PhD in business administration, psychology or a related field. Candidates with a set dissertation date may also apply.
A strong publication record in wellbeing science, including first-authored articles in leading international peer-reviewed journals
Documented expertise in language-based assessment of psychological constructs
Methodological and quantitative competence and programming in R and/or Python
Demonstrated research independence and an established international research network
Documented experience communicating research to non-academic audiences, e.g., media, public lectures or popular science

Meritorious
Experience with assessment methods beyond self-report, e.g., implicit measures or automated coding of text
Development of open research software or openly shared models
Applied collaborations with organizations or industry, e.g., in work-related wellbeing or psychometrics 

How to apply: 
Formal submission will be via the SSE Varbi online platform by latest December 15, 2026. The following documents should be included in your application: 
A curriculum vitae 
A separate document listing published articles (if any) and articles submitted to journals, as well as other academic peer-reviewed publications (e.g., book chapters, conference proceedings). 
Copies of representative research, that is, copies of your publications or work in progress (max 5) 
Evidence of stakeholder engagement, for example copies or links to blogs, opinion pieces, podcasts, LinkedIn posts 
Names and contact information for two people willing to provide references. 

We recommend that you apply as soon as possible and at the latest before December 15, 2026. Starting date is flexible but preferably around April 2027. The employment is postdoctoral employment of two years.

Our mission is to enable our DevOps teams to focus on building great applications by providing a shared internal developer platform, tools, templates and ways of working that simplify the entire software development lifecycle. Today, we support more than 20 teams across all three divisions, combining hands-on engineering with coaching, training and technical enablement.

Ultimately, our goal is simple: remove complexity, create great developer experiences and enable teams to deliver secure, high-quality software faster.

Role Description
As a Cloud Architect in CORE Platform, you will help shape the AWS foundation that our DevOps teams build on. Instead of every team solving the same cloud challenges themselves, we create reusable patterns, guardrails and infrastructure-as-code that make it easier to build, deploy and operate software securely and efficiently.

You will combine hands-on cloud engineering with architecture and enablement, designing and operating shared AWS capabilities while working closely with the teams that use them. Their challenges and feedback become input for better automation, self-service and reusable solutions across the organization.

Together with colleagues across Platform Engineering, Product and Security, you will help develop a coherent platform where reliability and security are built in from the start. You will also run Game Days, including sessions together with AWS, and use those learnings to continuously strengthen the platform.

Looking ahead, we are preparing for AI agents to become platform users alongside developers. You will have the opportunity to help shape the cloud patterns and secure environments that make that possible, while influencing how Husqvarna’s use of AWS evolves. What you will do:
Design and build reusable AWS patterns, templates and guardrails as code.
Ensure our cloud capabilities are reliable, secure and performant.
Improve automation and self-service based on the needs of our DevOps teams.
Run Game Days and turn learnings into concrete improvements.
Evolve our cloud patterns as AWS, technology and user needs change.
Coach and mentor engineers across teams.

5+ years of professional experience working with cloud technologies, with deep knowledge of AWS.

jobs.occupation: Embedded Engineer - System and Software | Scania Special Vehicles
jobs.description:
Scania is undergoing a transformation from being a leading supplier of trucks, buses, and engines to providing complete and sustainable transport solutions. Together with TRATON and our sister brands MAN, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International, we are working to shape the future of mobility with innovative and environmentally conscious solutions. 
Our values – customer first, respect, team spirit, responsibility, and elimination of waste – are at the heart of everything we do. Together, we are at the forefront of creating a sustainable future.
Role Summary
We are looking for an Embedded Engineer who enjoys technical challenges, hands-on development, and working across different vehicle systems. 
Scania Special Vehicles develops customer-specific solutions that go beyond our standard product offering. Within the System and Software group, we develop and integrate functions and systems for both defence and civilian vehicles. 
Our work is close to the product. We combine a prototyping mindset with production readiness, finding pragmatic solutions, testing them in vehicles and rigs, and ensuring they are robust enough for production and customer use. 
 
Our projects cover a broad range of vehicle systems, including: 

Defence: PHEV based on BEV3, navigation systems, tactical functions, Protected Cab, onboard diagnostics, and Central Tire Inflation Systems. 

Civilian: Scania Longline, BEV for mining, Super Heavy Haulage, City Door, and mixed suspension solutions. 

 
Job Responsibilities
As an Embedded Engineer, you will work across the complete development chain, from customer needs and requirements to system development, software implementation, integration, and verification. 
 
Your responsibilities will include: 
Developing and integrating embedded functions and vehicle systems.
Investigating existing systems and identifying pragmatic technical solutions.
Prototyping, testing, troubleshooting, and verifying solutions in vehicles and test rigs.
Adapting existing systems to meet customer-specific requirements.
Managing system change requests and coordinating necessary technical changes.
Taking solutions from initial concepts and prototypes to production-ready implementation.
Collaborating with different development teams and stakeholders across Scania. 

 
Our projects vary in size and technical content, and we often work on several in parallel. You should therefore enjoy a high and variable pace, short development loops, and the opportunity to work across different technical areas. 
 
Who You Are
We are looking for a curious and pragmatic engineer who enjoys understanding how systems work and finding solutions to technical challenges. 
You take ownership of your assignments, work well with others, and are comfortable investigating problems independently. You have a hands-on engineering mindset and enjoy seeing your solutions come to life in vehicles and test rigs. 
We believe you have:
A master's degree in mechatronics, physics, computer science, or another relevant engineering field.
Experience in embedded software and/or system development.
Experience in vehicle functions, electronics, or system integration.
Knowledge of CAN communication.
A hands-on approach to development and problem solving.
Good communication and collaboration skills.
Good English skills, both written and spoken. 

 
It is an advantage if you have experience with: 
Scania development processes and systems.
Scania vehicle architecture.
Vehicle diagnostics.
Electrification and electric vehicle systems. 

 
You do not need to be an expert in every vehicle system. What matters most is your technical curiosity, willingness to learn, and ability to take responsibility for finding a way forward. 
 
This Is Us
System and Software is part of Scania Special Vehicles. We work with customer-specific solutions that require flexibility, broad technical knowledge, and close cooperation across Scania. 
Our work combines technical investigations, hands-on development, and production-oriented engineering. We value practical solutions, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement. 
The variety of projects provides opportunities to develop your competence across different vehicle systems while contributing directly to vehicles delivered to our customers. 
In the System and Software group, we work closely together and support one another while also fostering independent thinking and technical depth. You'll find our group to be technically driven, customer-focused, and collaborative—where everyone has a voice and a real opportunity to shape both what we do and how we do it. 
Scania Offers
We offer a dynamic and engaging workplace where collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. You will be part of a strong team environment that encourages knowledge sharing and close cooperation across functions. 
With a structured development plan and a wide range of training opportunities, Scania supports your professional growth both locally and internationally. 
Benefits include access to our health center in Gröndal or a wellness allowance, result bonus, flexible working hours, and company car leasing. Scania also arranges events for employees and their families, and for those living in Stockholm, convenient commuting is supported through direct Scania Job express buses to Södertälje
 
Application
We look forward to receiving your application, consisting of your CV and kindly ask you not to share a cover letter to ensure an efficient and unbiased recruitment process for all parties. 
Apply as soon as possible, no later than 2026-11-21. Screening will take place on an ongoing basis during the application period. Logical and personality tests may be used as part of the selection process, and a background check may be required for this role. 
If you have questions or would like more information, please contact: Mascarenhas Murilo, murilo.mascarenhas@scania.com, Head of System and Software 

 
We look forward to your application!
